direction_convention.why: The audited endpoint direction of every cross-connect tier is a 2-source/2-target braid. In tb the frozen router refuses that braid in every view (raw refusals in checks/*-a1-tb-check.txt) because a tb rank gap leaves three routing lanes for four independently-routed links. lr gives the gap a label-sized channel (lib gap rule: channel = max(3 + ceil(crossings/2), longest_label + 4)), which routes the braid with one bridge per tier, the structural minimum. Nothing else changed between attempt 1 and attempt 2 in any view.
direction_convention.cost: lr cannot express vertical elevation, so the source's 'spine above leaf' correction is not shown (defect D1).

arrow_convention: Every arrow is a physical link trace drawn from the relationship's first-listed endpoint to its second-listed endpoint exactly as the case audit states it (ispA -> mux1 ... leaf2 -> rack2). No arrow implies one-way traffic, and no endpoint was reversed to force a layout.

known_defects.defect: The source correction 'border leaf and leaf at the same height; spine above the leaf' is not honored. Ranks read left to right as border leaf -> spine -> rack leaf, so the spines sit between the two leaf tiers instead of above them.
known_defects.evidence: v3 frame 0: Spine 1 x=16, Leaf 1 x=34 (spines left of the rack leaves); v2 frame 0: BL 1 x=43, Spine 2 x=61 (spines right of the border leaves)
known_defects.why_not_fixed: expressing it needs either reversed endpoint direction (forbidden by the case's fixed constraints) or explicit placement (excluded by round-05's engine-owned placement rule); tb refuses to route these tiers at all (see blocker B1)

known_defects.defect: Within-rank vertical order is not stable across views: v2 draws Spine 2 above Spine 1, v3 draws Spine 1 above Spine 2.
known_defects.evidence: v2 frame 0 Spine 2 at y=16 and Spine 1 at y=26; v3 frame 0 Spine 1 at y=16 and Spine 2 at y=26
known_defects.why: the engine orders each rank by neighbour barycenter, and the two views have different neighbours; ordering is engine-owned and was not reordered by hand

known_defects.defect: Dash style is only provable on straight segments; corner and elbow glyphs (╭ ╮ ⌒) are shared between solid and dashed routes, so the standby style is proven by the straight dashed runs plus the standby? label text, not by the corners.

blockers.blocker: The frozen binary's router refuses the tb (top-down) orientation of every 2x2 cross-connect tier in this topology: 'no obstacle-safe route for <edge>; increase node/layer spacing'. Each view's tb attempt was rejected before any check output existed.
raw_refusals: checks/v1-a1-tb-check.txt: rataflow-view: no obstacle-safe route for mux2 -> core1; increase node/layer spacing
checks/v2-a1-tb-check.txt: rataflow-view: no obstacle-safe route for core2 -> fw2, fw1 -> bl1, bl2 -> sp2; increase node/layer spacing
checks/v3-a1-tb-check.txt: rataflow-view: no obstacle-safe route for sp2 -> leaf1, leaf2 -> rack2; increase node/layer spacing
blockers.classification: genuine renderer limitation for this case, not a spec error: nodes, edges, labels and groups were unchanged between the refused tb spec and the routed lr spec in each view, and the only lever left inside the rules was direction
blockers.workaround_used: lr, which routed all three views with one bridge per braid tier

blockers.blocker: Capability gap: no spec field controls node box height, so the source's request to reduce individual box height (line 166) cannot be expressed.
blockers.impact: box height stays at the engine's 5 rows; the compactness requests are met only through view splitting and extents (45x39, 68x20, 49x20)
